title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This page is a typed exercise sheet, page 2 of a problem in elementary real and complex analysis, in French. It is unrelated to the surrounding handwritten notes on divided-power De Rham complexes. Those notes concern truncation and adjunction functors τ_N, φ_N, q_N on graded module categories. The sheet was most likely bound into the folder by accident or reused as scrap; it plausibly comes from Grothendieck's undergraduate teaching at Montpellier. The setting is a sequence c_n ≥ 0 decreasing to 0, and series of the form Σ u_n c_n whose partial sums S_n = Σ_{k≤n} u_k stay bounded. This is Abel/Dirichlet summation, referred to as (1). (c) End of a part on periodic sequences. Certain sequences u(s), together with the constant sequence 1, form a basis of the space E_r of complex sequences of period r. The series Σ u(s)_n c_n is alternating with decreasing absolute values tending to 0, so it converges by the Leibniz test. This gives a second proof of (b). Presumably (b) says Σ u_n c_n converges for every r-periodic u with zero mean over a period. (d) Take u_n = z^n for n ≥ 1. The partial sums S_n stay bounded iff (5) holds: |z| ≤ 1 and z ≠ 1. In that case |S_n| ≤ 2|z|/|1−z|. Consequently Σ c_n z^n converges on E = {|z| ≤ 1, z ≠ 1}. It converges absolutely for |z| < 1. On |z| = 1, z ≠ 1, it converges absolutely iff Σ c_n converges. For A ⊂ E, convergence is uniform on A if |1−z| ≥ a > 0 on A. This condition is also necessary when Σ c_n diverges. When Σ c_n converges, convergence is uniform on the whole closed disc. (e) f(z) = Σ c_n z^n is continuous on E. f has a finite limit at z = 1 iff Σ c_n converges; then f is continuous on the closed unit disc (an Abel-type theorem). (f) Application to Σ c_n e^{inx}, Σ c_n cos nx and Σ c_n sin nx. These converge for x ∉ 2πZ and define continuous functions on R − 2πZ. (g) (z^n) is r-periodic iff z^r = 1. Combined with (b), Σ c_n z^n converges at every root of unity except z = 1 when Σ c_n diverges. All of this is standard textbook material, the Dirichlet test and the Abel theorem.
errors: No mathematical errors. The bound 2|z|/|1−z| is correct, since S_n = z(1−z^n)/(1−z). The 'iff' statements in (d) and (e) are correct given c_n ≥ 0 decreasing to 0. The necessity of |1−z| ≥ a when Σ c_n diverges follows by letting z → 1 in the uniform Cauchy criterion. The final sentence of (g) is cut off at the bottom of the page.

missed.claim: Archival note only: a typed undergraduate analysis exercise sheet is misfiled or reused among the 1976 divided-power De Rham notes. It is evidence of Grothendieck's Montpellier teaching material, not new mathematics.

transcription_corrections: 'pour n 1' should read 'pour n ≥ 1'; '(z^n)_n 1' should read '(z^n)_{n≥1}'.
Series should carry Σ throughout: Σ u(s)_n c_n, Σ c_n z^n, f(z) = Σ c_n z^n, Σ c_n, Σ c_n e^{inx}, Σ c_n cos nx, Σ c_n sin nx.
'pour z 1' (absolute convergence) should read 'pour |z| < 1'; 'z = 1, z≠1' should read '|z| = 1, z ≠ 1'.
'z A' should read 'z ∈ A'; 'a 0' should read 'a > 0'; '1−z a' should read '|1−z| ≥ a'; 'z 1' (uniform convergence, closed disc) should read '|z| ≤ 1'.
'2 Z' should read '2πZ'; '2 n' should read '2πn'; 'x R − 2 Z' should read 'x ∈ R − 2πZ'.
Last line: 'dauf' should read 'sauf'; the series is Σ c_n z^n; the sentence is cut off after 'c_n' (presumably 'Σ c_n est divergente').
